examples.name: Sample — one label column, two value blocks
paragraphs: A quarterly summary printed as one row-label column on the left — Revenue, Gross profit, Selling, general and administrative expenses, EBIT, Non-controlling interests, Net income — feeding two separately boxed value blocks: C$ millions and (% of revenue), each with its own Q2 2025 / Q2 2024 header pair.

The right-hand block has no row labels of its own. Read on its own it is ten unnamed values, which is the proof that the two fragments were never meant to stand apart. The same structure is printed again below for the year-to-date figures, with its header rows repeated, so that block is a second table.

The blocks do not share a header row: each has its own. It is the label column that is printed once — the mirror sub-case. The em-dashes in the Non-controlling interests rows are values, not blanks (Marks and Symbols in Cells§9.6.6), and (% of revenue) is a units line in the header (Units Row§9.3.5). The empty gutter between the blocks is not a column (Gutter Columns§9.4.1).

examples.name: Sample — a numbered note heading in the gap
paragraphs: The four-column header (Consolidated / Merevald Retail Ltd, two dates each) is printed once at the top. Note 20 Reserves and note 21 Total equity reconciliation both sit under it, separated by the second note's heading. Neither fragment repeats the header, so it is one table, and each note heading is a band row inside it.
